basis: C6's 602/672 K and 586/672 Y_ind rates are observations from a different seed block and are not baseline-availability proxies. They do not establish C1 feasibility.

The C1 denominator is four target rows, so the 0.95 floor is a 100% rule (3/4 = 0.75). C4 would add at most 59-60 non-target rows per seed, giving an upper bound of 63-64 C1 rows; the observed denominator can be lower and may fall below the 60-row floor.
All six seeds having all four K rows is 6.9% under independence; the design is fragile, not merely underpowered.

c1_power_curve.model: Independent Bernoulli retention on each row; the stated retention rate q is common to A- and K-; a seed passes only when both arms meet 0.95; all-six assumes independent seeds. The separate correlation_sensitivity block relaxes the path and seed independence.
assumptions: The retention rate is an assumption, not an A1 measurement.
Rows are independent and identically distributed within an arm.
A- and K- have the same assumed retention rate and are independent.
The six seeds are independent; the all-six column is the product of six per-seed probabilities.
The gate is evaluated per seed; no pooling across seeds is used.

cliff_60.explanation: At 59 rows, 57/59 = 0.9661 and only two losses pass; at 60 rows, 57/60 = 0.95 and three losses pass. The extra row crosses a loss boundary in the gate arithmetic, not an empirical effect.

required_retention.assumption: Required q under the same independent Bernoulli, six-independent-seed model.

power_design_criterion.status: RECORDED — C1 DESIGN CRITERION; NOT AN OBSERVED RETENTION AND NOT A SECOND ACCEPTANCE GATE
power_design_criterion.denominator_kind: UPPER BOUND — NOT AN OBSERVED OR ESTIMATED BASELINE-AVAILABILITY DENOMINATOR
power_design_criterion.model: Independent Bernoulli retention on each row, with the six seeds independent, as in the required-retention table.
power_design_criterion.meaning: At the upper-bound 63-row scenario, reaching 80% all-six-seed power requires a common retention of at least 0.984017. The corresponding values are 0.984271 at 64 rows and 0.983204 at the 60-row floor. This sizes the planned design; it is not an observed retention and is not a second post-run acceptance gate. The observed-run acceptance rule remains the 0.95 preservation threshold.

correlation_sensitivity.status: SENSITIVITY — NOT AN OBSERVED CORRELATION OR RESULT
correlation_sensitivity.model: Gaussian copulas on the pass/fail indicators. Within a seed, the A- and K- pass indicators have correlation rho_paths; across seeds, the per-seed pass indicators have equicorrelation rho_seeds through one shared factor. Per-arm marginals remain the independent Bernoulli probabilities. The copulas are applied sequentially; no path-specific cross-seed correlation is added beyond the seed factor.
assumptions: The retention rate q is common to A- and K- and is an assumption, not a measurement.
Within an arm, rows remain independent and identically distributed.
rho_paths is a positive Gaussian-copula correlation between the A- and K- pass indicators; it is not estimated from A1.
rho_seeds is a positive one-factor Gaussian-copula correlation across the six seed-pass indicators; it is not estimated from A1.
The seed copula is applied to the per-seed joint pass probability; it does not model a separate path-specific seed effect.
The gate remains per seed and all-six; correlation changes the joint probability, not the marginal gate rule.
correlation_sensitivity.reading: At n=63 and q=.95, independent paths and independent seeds give a per-seed pass probability of 0.375577 and an all-six probability of 0.002807. A path correlation of .5 raises the per-seed probability to 0.453562; a seed correlation of .5 raises the all-six probability to 0.073188; both at .5 give 0.113341. Positive correlation makes the six seeds share their fate: all-six can rise while the chance that none pass also rises. These are sensitivity scenarios, not correlation estimates.

denominator_floor_rule.adopted_together: 60-row denominator floor and C1/C4 post-freeze VOID gate
denominator_floor_rule.unit: minimum paired-control available rows across all six seeds and both A- and K- paths
denominator_floor_rule.why: At 59 rows, 57/59 = 0.9661 and only two losses pass; at 60 rows, 57/60 = 0.95 and three losses pass. 60 is the first denominator with the planned three-loss tolerance.
denominator_floor_rule.decision: If the observed minimum is below 60 on any seed or path, the A1 run is VOID — C1_DENOMINATOR_BELOW_FLOOR, before any model is read.
denominator_floor_rule.perfect_59: A perfect 59/59 is still VOID: the fraction cannot rescue a denominator below the resolution floor.
denominator_floor_rule.not_parked: PARKED is for a missing target set or grant. This is an executed run whose planned resolution was not reached, so it is VOID.
denominator_floor_rule.not_identified: No model verdict is read. VOID is not NOT IDENTIFIED.
denominator_floor_rule.below_20: Below 20 rows even one loss fails; the denominator is too small to express the 0.95 criterion and the same VOID applies.
denominator_floor_rule.above_planned: A denominator above 64 is a design inconsistency: score only the preplanned rows and do not add rows after the fact.

c1_power_curve.reading: At a true retention of 0.95, the 63-row upper-bound scenario gives a 61.3% chance for one arm, 37.6% for both arms on one seed, and 0.3% across all six seeds. At 0.98, the corresponding all-six chance is 63.2%. A denominator of 20 is the smallest listed value that can still pass with one lost row.

availability_budget.rule: max_unavailable_rows = candidate_rows - floor; required_availability_fraction = floor / candidate_rows
availability_budget.note: Denominator-floor arithmetic on the candidate-count upper bound; not an observed or estimated baseline-availability rate.
availability_budget.retention_rule: The separate 0.95 C1 retention rule allows three losses at 60-64; availability is counted first and is not part of that allowance.

c1_denominator_feasibility.why: The 63-64 rows are the candidate-universe counts, not a measurement of edges available in the paired A+K+ control. C1 counts only those available rows. The observed denominator can be lower than 63-64; if the minimum is below 60 on any seed or path, the run is VOID before any model is read.

unrelated_observations.reason: These percentages come from different seed blocks, different world populations and different quantities. None measures paired-control availability in the A1 target universe, so none may be used to estimate, bound or certify the C1 denominator.

findings.finding: The 24 targets are statistically indistinguishable from the 358 unselected candidates on cycle-36 strength.
Cycle membership and positive U do not narrow the candidate universe; every candidate is eligible.
C6 reports high K/Y_ind prevalence in its own seed block. This is a different-world observation, not a C1 baseline-availability measurement and not a target-validation proxy.
With four target rows, the 0.95 C1 floor is effectively 100% preservation; one lost row gives 0.75.

Even if every candidate edge were baseline-available, C4 plus the four target rows would produce at most 63-64 C1 rows per seed. This is an upper bound, not an observed or estimated denominator; unavailable rows reduce it and can push the run below the 60-row floor.

decision.verdict: FREEZE READINESS OPEN — C1 DENOMINATOR FRAGILITY
decision.reading: P0 and feasibility pass, but four target rows per seed make the precommitted 0.95 C1 floor a 100% preservation rule. C6's K/Y_ind prevalence is a different-seed observation and does not establish C1 baseline availability. The 63-64 C1 figure is an upper bound, not an estimate; the observed denominator can be lower and may fail the 60-row floor. C1 remains unmeasured; do not freeze on the current target artifact.
